prediction.likelyOutcome: U.S. Bank is very likely to obtain both the foreclosure judgment and the in personam money judgment given the undisputed loan documents, the admitted Covid-era default, and the borrower's failure to object to the combined pleading structure; the main open question going into the bench trial is what, if anything, the two years of contested liability litigation have produced by way of a forbearance-related or payment-application defense that could shave some amount (interest, fees, or a partial credit) off the full $46,290,900.25 figure pleaded. Expect a judgment at or very near the complaint's stated amount, plus some additional interest/fees under the loan documents that cannot be quantified from this record.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court held Penn Realty breached the loan agreement and entered an in personam money judgment for U.S. Bank of $51,392,086.96 (no judgment in mortgage foreclosure was entered); the Third Circuit affirmed that judgment in a separate unpublished opinion (No. 23-2185, Sept. 25, 2024). In this precedential appeal the Third Circuit upheld the subsequent execution sale of the apartment building under Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a) and affirmed the denial of the borrower's motion to quash.
